Add a Fix-Up to a Change-Set Log

Source: R/rProject-fix-up.R
FixUp.Rd

A fix-up is a small push after a change set was logged (the upload folder is final, so a later change is a new push). FixUp() appends a ## Fix-up: <summary> section to the newest log for topic: the commit message skeleton (ending Log: .setup/logs/<log>) and the lists of files to update in Overleaf, compared with the clone of the private repository (the same rules as Log()). It also adds a pending row to the log's "Pushes" table (in the order of the table's header) and a pending row to .setup/logs/index.md. After the push, Verify() with record = TRUE fills them in. Upload() with fixup = TRUE builds the upload folder.

Usage

FixUp(path, topic, summary, private = file.path(path, ".verify"))

Arguments

path

Character string. Project path.

topic

Character string. Short topic in kebab case (e.g., "log-spec"). The change-set log uses the same topic.

summary

Character string. First line of the fix-up's commit message.

private

Character string. Path to a clone of the private repository at the pushed commit. By default .verify in the project.

Value

Returns the path of the log invisibly.

Author

Ivan Jacob Agaloos Pesigan

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
FixUp(path = getwd(), topic = "my-topic", summary = "Fix-up: handoff")
} # }
